verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Floating in the Pacific Ocean... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego on April 10'; R3: 'splashed down into the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm splashdown location in Pacific off San Diego coast and date aligns with April 10 from R2 and mission timeline.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft capsule is named "Integrity".
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly states the name of the Orion spacecraft as 'Integrity'.

verifications.claim: The capsule named "Integrity" touched down at approximately 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time'; R2: 'just past 8 p.m. EDT / 5 p.m. PDT'; R3: 'touched down at 5.07pm'
verifications.reasoning: Time matches across sources (5:07 p.m. PDT = 8:07 p.m. EDT), and R2 confirms 'Integrity' name.

verifications.claim: The splashdown concluded a 10-day mission around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'After 10 days'; R3: 'officially 9 days 1hr and 32min... recorded officially as a 10-day mission'; R1: implies via launch April 1 and travel distance
verifications.reasoning: R2 and R3 explicitly state 10-day mission; R1 supports via timeline.

verifications.claim: The splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean roughly 60 miles off the San Diego coast.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: References confirm Pacific off San Diego but no mention of 'roughly 60 miles' distance.

verifications.claim: The splashdown time was April 10, 2026, at 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m. Eastern time'; R2: 'April 10 just past 8 p.m. EDT / 5 p.m. PDT'; R3: 'April 10... 5.07pm'
verifications.reasoning: Date from R2/R3, precise time confirmed across all with correct timezone conversion.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew included Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and CSA specialist Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'; R2/R3: exact roles and names match
verifications.reasoning: All sources list identical crew members with matching roles.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew was recovered by the U.S. Navy and recovery teams.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery team... U.S.S. John P. Murtha'; R2: 'US Navy divers... USS John P. Murtha'; R3: 'recovery crew from the USS John P Murtha... navy personnel'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm U.S. Navy and recovery teams handled crew recovery.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marked the first crewed return from the moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first people to leave low-Earth orbit since 1972'; R2: 'first... around the moon in more than 50 years'; R3: 'first humans... since Apollo 17 in December 1972'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed lunar flyby/return since 1972 (over 50 years in 2026).

verifications.claim: The capsule was welcomed by recovery teams including Navy EODGRU-1 and USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: References mention recovery teams and USS John P. Murtha but no mention of 'Navy EODGRU-1'.
